text:
Maria G.: noticing a ~50-120ms p99 bump on a handful of hosts during the noon traffic surge, looks correlated with KV eviction churn
Tom H.: which policy? LRU or FIFO?
Maria G.: LRU on these machines (default). spike aligns with heavy long-context requests (20-30k tokens) + large batching bursts
Kevin L.: hmm. could be reuse window collapse + paging. any logs from the pager/evicter?
Maria G.: pasted minimal log snippet below from node-7 at 12:34:10 — see repeated 'evict' + 'pager-scan' entries around the latency spike
Maria G.: ```
[12:34:09.987] evicter: candidate 0x7f12 size=512k age=120s reuse=0.3 policy=lru
[12:34:09.988] pager: trigger page-out scanned=48 reclaimed=0
[12:34:10.002] latency: request_id=3f2a p99=230ms kv_wait=120ms
[12:34:10.050] evicter: reinsert failed due to frag-split, tombstone-insert policy=fifo_compatible
```
Tom H.: interesting that reinsert failed — fragmentation + tombstone churn can make evicter do extra scans. could be a correctness/regression where we try to reinsert into a slot still marked for paging
Kevin L.: also check kernel selection: if kernels pick slower matmul paths under long seqs, combined with blocking evictions can surface as perceived KV latency. but logs show kv_wait is main culprit
Maria G.: reproduction steps: run long-context mixture (50% 8k, 50% 25k) with batch-size spikes (simulate traffic bursts) against a node with 48GB KV arena; observe p99 growing after ~5-10m
Tom H.: can you dump evicter counters (scan_count, reinserts, fragmentation_rate) and the per-arena free list histogram?
Maria G.: dumping now, pushing to the thread in a sec.
infra-bot: deploybot: rolled back candidate runtime v1.4.2 on node-7 at 12:36 due to alerts :warning:
Kevin L.: rollback helps isolate whether a recent evicter change caused this. any code commits around reinsertion logic in last deploy?
Tom H.: I bisected locally — a change to reinsertion backoff landed in 1.4.2 (PR #4123). it altered the eviction handshake to prefer FIFO fallbacks when reinserts hit fragmentation. maybe we regress reuse semantics.
Maria G.: that matches: we see more FIFO path entries in the logs. but the FIFO fallback seems to flip ordering and cause a replay storm under bursty batches
Kevin L.: hypotheses: (1) reinsertion backoff reduces successful reuse -> more cold hits -> more paging -> elevated p99 (2) FIFO fallback creates ordering that starves hot chains causing extra scans
Tom H.: quick experiment: force LRU-only path (toggle env KV_EVICT_FORCE_LRU=1) on a canary and replay the workload for 10m. if p99 goes down we have a smoking gun.
Maria G.: doing that now on node-9. also enabling kv_reuse_trace=1 to capture reuse decisions.
Maria G.: initial canary numbers after 3m: p99 back to baseline, kv_wait down from 120ms->15ms, reinserts_success up 4x, fragmentation_rate slightly lower
Kevin L.: that's pretty convincing. still need to check correctness edgecases — why did the FIFO fallback exist? probably to avoid starvation in some allocation pattern. might be a heuristic that misfires under heavy long-context + large batching
Tom H.: action items:
- Maria: keep canary up and collect full perf counters + heap histo (assigned)
- Kevin: audit PR #4123 reinsertion backoff logic for ordering hazards (assigned)
- Tom: run controlled stress harness to reproduce with both LRU and FIFO forced (assigned)
Maria G.: noted. I'll upload traces and perf maps to https://artifacts.redwood/kv/1755559999/ by EOD :eyes:
Kevin L.: if confirmed, revert PR or tweak heuristic to consider reuse_score threshold before switching to FIFO
Tom H.: +1. also let's add a regression test in kv-simulator that includes long-context mix + bursty batching so this doesn't silently slip again :rocket:
Maria G.: thanks all — keeping thread updated with traces and a short postmortem once we have root cause
Tom H.: thx, will standby to review the revert/patch. :thumbsup:
